one_line_contribution: It claims the raw-vs-distilled memory disagreement is not about abstraction level at all but about two nameable content classes inside items — source-scene object-to-receptacle bindings (valuable only when the deployment scene overlaps the training scene, harmful otherwise) and failure-to-repair pairs (scene-invariant) — and it tests this causally by transplanting each cue into and out of six representations at matched injected-token budgets, predicting that representation identity has no residual effect once the two cue indicators are conditioned on.
closest_prior_work: SkillEvolBench, arXiv:2605.24117 (verified via the literature command; its indexed abstract reads 'raw trajectory reuse often outperforming distilled skills due to discarded contextual cues'). This is the sharpest threat precisely because the proposal is its direct sequel: the causal story — distillation discards contextual cues, and that is why raw wins — is already asserted in the prior work's own abstract. The delta here is naming two specific cue classes, transplanting them, and splitting by scene overlap, which SkillEvolBench does not do (no token-matched comparison, no seen/unseen split, no cue identification). That is a real but bounded advance: the headline framing is inherited, and what is new is one notch of mechanism. Two further papers erode the framing. arXiv:2608.15008 'Harness the Memory: A Holistic Evaluation of Memory Substrates in Memory Agents' (verified) already reports a controlled harness over text records, structural stores, hierarchical stores and refinement-based memories finding regime-dependent trade-offs and that no substrate dominates — i.e. 'the abstraction/substrate is not the operative variable' is partly published, though without cue-level attribution or transplants. The proposal cites this ID in Related Work as 'substrate routing' but never confronts it as a competitor for its central framing. arXiv:2603.02473 'Diagnosing Retrieval vs. Utilization Bottlenecks in LLM Agent Memory' (found in my search, not verified with the paper command) reports raw chunk storage matching or exceeding fact extraction and summarization, and attributes variance to the retrieval method rather than the write representation — an independent partial pre-emption of P5's null. SEC itself I verified as a real non-arXiv paper: Semantic Scholar indexes 'Experience Retrieval Compression for Continual Adaptation of LLM Agents' (AIEA 2026, 2 citations) with the four-field unit of task type, key decisions, failure reason and repair action exactly as described.
strongest_objection: The two named cues are not orthogonal to a simpler explanation the design cannot rule out: procedure copying from a near-duplicate demonstration. On ALFWorld, 'seen scene, different task instance' tasks in the same room share object types, receptacle inventory and admissible-action phrasing, so a retrieved same-room raw trajectory is close to a step-by-step solution the agent can imitate. Raw's seen-scene advantage may therefore be action-sequence copyability, not the binding fact. The load-bearing ablation makes this worse rather than better: minus-B replaces receptacle identities with placeholders, which simultaneously (a) removes the binding content, (b) destroys the copyable action sequence, since the actions are 'go to fridge / open fridge', and (c) degrades the item's surface fluency and parsability. So a confirmed P2 is equally consistent with the binding hypothesis, the procedure-copying hypothesis, and plain text corruption, and the decoy control only isolates token load, not any of these. The proposal half-knows this — action ordering is pre-registered as a third cue — but only as a contingency triggered by a residual in P5, i.e. it is tested only if the main claim has already failed, which is backwards for a competing explanation of the primary result. A related but secondary version of the same problem: all distilled forms are written by the 27B while the pool and the primary evaluation are on the 120B, so the raw-vs-distilled gap magnitude is partly a writer-capability artifact (the transplant arms mitigate this for the mechanism claim but not for P1's effect size). Second-order but real: P3 assumes foreign bindings are wrong, yet AI2-THOR receptacle semantics are stereotyped across rooms (food in fridges, utensils in drawers), so a foreign binding is often approximately correct; a null on P3 would then be read as 'bindings do not matter' when the true reading is 'the manipulation was weak'.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Promote the procedure-copying cue to a third arm of the main factorial rather than a fallback: add minus-P (permute or paraphrase the action sequence while keeping receptacle names intact) crossed with minus-B, so binding content and copyable procedure are separated in the confirmatory run rather than after it. 2) Implement minus-B as a consistent re-labeling with valid-but-wrong receptacle names drawn from the same vocabulary, not as placeholders, so surface form, fluency and token count are preserved and only the referent changes. 3) Add the missing scene-agnostic prior control (see missing_baseline). 4) Replace P5's 'residual within MDE' with a pre-registered equivalence test (TOST) whose bound is tied to the effect being explained — e.g. 30 percent of the measured raw-vs-insight seen-scene gap — because a 4-point residual declared 'within a 5-point MDE' would be the same order as SEC's published +7.7 and would not support 'abstraction per se is inert'; and report attenuation-corrected cue coefficients using the error rate from the 200-item annotator audit, since noisy binary cue indicators under-adjust and inflate the residual the proposal wants to show is zero. 5) State up front that ALFWorld already ships valid-seen and valid-unseen splits and give per-split n; the risk section's framing ('a room-level split may need to be by room type') reads as though this were an open problem and invites doubt about whether the primary contrast is even constructible. 6) Run at least one distilled arm with the 120B as writer to bound the writer-capability confound. 7) Given the budget, drop the WebShop analogue (admittedly loose) and the R4/R6 arms before dropping seeds.
missing_baseline: A scene-agnostic aggregate binding prior: a 60-token receptacle prior mined over ALL training scenes ('apples are usually in the fridge, knives in the drawer') rather than from the source scene, injected in the same slot and at the same token count as the plus-B table. Without it, a confirmed P2 cannot distinguish 'the agent needs THIS scene's bindings' from 'the agent needs ANY receptacle prior and the source-scene table happens to be a correct instance of one' — and the foreign-binding arm does not cover this, since foreign bindings are specific-and-wrong whereas an aggregate prior is general-and-mostly-right. This control is also what makes the paper's practical claim land or collapse: if a scene-agnostic 60-token prior recovers most of raw's seen-scene advantage, the whole seen/unseen framing is deflated into 'ALFWorld agents lack a commonsense receptacle prior'. A cheaper second omission: a bindings-only memory (the 60-token table with no trajectory, insight or record around it) as the token-efficiency upper bound; the instruction-slot arm approximates this but confounds slot with content.

Judgement of the proposal's own check: it is well above the average for this pipeline — four queries reported with IDs, the closest named method correctly identified and its claim quoted, SEC's venue correctly identified as a non-arXiv conference paper, and the empty seen/unseen query honestly reported as empty rather than spun as novelty, with the failed channels (WebSearch budget exhausted, S2 HTTP 429) disclosed. Its one substantive gap is that it never searched the memory-substrate/representation-comparison family, so it cites 2608.15008 in Related Work as 'substrate routing' without ever asking whether 'no substrate dominates' collides with 'abstraction is not the operative variable', and it missed 2603.02473 entirely. Novelty is scored on the verified position: the premise is published, the cue-level attribution is not.
